title: quantization-exec-path-specs-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-draft-v4
content:
Purpose:
This document captures the execution-path constraints, kernel compatibility requirements, and scheduling/KV-cache implications for supporting multiple quantization families in the Redwood serving runtime. Focus is on INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ execution paths for transformer-style models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder), with concrete kernel constraints, fallback behavior, and testing requirements.

Scope:
- Define per-quant format kernel constraints (memory layout, block sizes, alignment, fused operations) that the runtime and kernel runner must enforce.
- Identify how scheduling/batching and KV cache management change across quant families.
- Specify compatibility and fallback rules between quantized and non-quantized model variants.
- Outline a validation/test plan and outstanding questions for follow-up.

Background and goals:
Redwood’s serving runtime must support rapid switching between model variants (e.g., FP16 -> INT8 -> AWQ) based on routing policies (cost vs latency). Quantized kernels introduce constraints that affect memory layout, fused op availability, and KV cache layout. Our goals are:
1) Define a minimal, enforceable contract for kernels so the scheduler can reason about capacity and compatibility.
2) Minimize unexpected runtime fallbacks and ensure graceful degradation when an optimized kernel is unavailable.
3) Preserve KV cache correctness across mixed-precision and quantization-crossing scenarios.

Assumptions:
- Models are stored with metadata indicating quant family, scale/zero-point or per-channel quant params, and any layout transformation applied at training/export time.
- Kernel implementations will expose a capability vector (see "Kernel capability contract") describing supported ops and constraints.
- Scheduler has access to model and kernel metadata at route-time and can select a compatible execution path or fallback.

Kernel capability contract (required fields):
Every kernel implementation must provide a capability descriptor (flattened key/value strings exposed to the runtime):
- quant_family: one of [FP16, FP8, INT8, GPTQ, AWQ, BF16, FP32]
- supported_block_size: comma-separated list of block sizes (e.g., "512,256")
- requires_contiguous_weights: "true" | "false"
- per_channel_scales: "true" | "false"
- supports_decoder_cross_attention: "true" | "false"
- supports_kv_fp_storage: "FP16" | "FP32" | "same_as_weights" | "compact_int"
- max_seq_len_single_tensor: integer (as string)
- fused_ops: comma-separated list (e.g., "gelu,layernorm,quant_dequant")
- supports_batched_kv_rewrite: "true" | "false"
- memory_alignment_bytes: integer (as string)
- quant_block_stride_bytes: integer (as string)
- kernel_version: string

Per-quant family constraints and notes:
1) INT8
- Weight layout: typically row-wise int8 with per-channel scale (s_i) and optional zero point. We require kernels to accept either per-channel asymmetric quantization or symmetric per-channel depending on implementation.
- Block sizes: optimized kernels expect block-aligned hidden dims; supported_block_size should include 128/256/512. If model hidden_size is not a supported size, runtime must either pad weights at load time (preferred for hosted) or mark model incompatible for that kernel.
- Memory alignment: 64-byte alignment recommended; memory_alignment_bytes must be present.
- KV cache: stores activations in FP16 by default for retokenization and mixing with other variants; some INT8 kernels support compact int KV storage ("compact_int"). If kernel advertises supports_kv_fp_storage != "compact_int", runtime must perform on-the-fly dequant->FP16 conversion for KV writes and readback.
- Fused ops: many INT8 kernels include quantize/dequantize fused into matmuls; descriptor must list fused_ops so runtime can avoid double-quantization.
- Determinism: INT8 paths may increase non-determinism; tests must include numeric-tolerance thresholds.

2) FP8
- FP8 formats (e.g., E4M3, E5M2) must be encoded in kernel descriptor: quant_subformat: e.g., "E4M3".
- FP8 has dynamic range differences and sometimes requires explicit scaling at GEMM-level. Kernels must expose whether they keep accumulators in FP16/FP32. supports_kv_fp_storage should typically be "same_as_weights" or FP16.
- Block sizes: similar to INT8 but often require different alignment; include memory_alignment_bytes.
- Mixed precision: FP8 kernels often require special layernorm/softmax implementations to preserve stability; fused_ops should indicate which layers are covered.
- KV cache: FP8 is not ideal for long-lived KV accumulation; prefer storing KV in FP16/FP32. If a kernel advertises FP8-stored KV, it must also guarantee rounding semantics and provide read/write conversion latency numbers.

3) GPTQ (post-training quantization targeting 4- or 8-bit)
- Format: GPTQ ensembles often produce a compressed weight layout (e.g., scale + codebook) and require a custom dequant codelet. Descriptor should include weight_encoding: e.g., "gptq_4bit_blockwise" and codelet_version.
- Block constraints: GPTQ often uses blockwise quantization (e.g., 32 or 64 columns); supported_block_size must list these.
- Runtime overhead: GPTQ dequant needs additional CPU/GPU ops at load-time or per-inference depending on kernel design. Kernel descriptor must include dequant_runtime_cost_ms_per_layer (string).
- KV cache: GPTQ weights generally require dequant to FP16 before matmul; KV cache storage should be FP16 in runtime unless kernel explicitly supports compressed-kv.
- Compatibility: GPTQ kernels are rarely interchangeable with INT8/AWQ; scheduler must treat GPTQ families as distinct.

4) AWQ (Activation-aware quantization / adaptive weight quantization)
- Format: AWQ sometimes uses heterogeneous bitwidth per-channel; descriptor must include per_channel_bitwidths_supported: "true"|"false" and max_bits.
- Kernel constraints: AWQ kernels may require specific reorderings (e.g., column-major with channel blocks). supported_block_size must reflect that.
- KV cache: similar to GPTQ, prefer FP16 storage of KV. If kernel supports compact_kv, descriptor must provide conversion latencies.
- Fallbacks: AWQ kernels may gracefully fall back to per-matrix dequant to FP16 at slight throughput loss; provide fallback_cost_estimate in descriptor.

Scheduling and batch planning implications:
- Kernel compatibility grouping: scheduler must group backfilled requests by compatible capability vectors. Compatibility is exact-match for quant_family and functional superset for fused_ops and supported_block_size.
- Packing policy: for INT8/FP8 paths that support continuous batching, we allow inter-request packing only when all requests share quant_family and kv_storage expectations.
- Mixed model routing: when routing policies want to prefer lower-cost kernels (e.g., INT8) but model variant is FP16, scheduler may elect to route to INT8-quantized artifact only if the model has an INT8 export and the kernel capability includes required fused_ops.
- Pre-warm vs on-demand: some GPTQ/AWQ kernels have high per-run dequant overhead; scheduler should prefer pre-warmed workers for these families. Descriptor field dequant_runtime_cost_ms_per_layer and prewarm_recommendation: "true" | "false" should be respected.
- Autoscaling signals: performance counters for quant kernels might be different (e.g., lower GPU utilization but higher memory bandwidth). Expose per-kernel perf counters so autoscaler can make informed decisions.

KV cache semantics and constraints:
- Canonical KV storage in runtime: FP16 by default (compatibility and numeric stability). Kernels that provide compact-kv must specify the storage format and conversion costs.
- Cross-variant reuse: If a request writes KV using one kernel format (e.g., FP16) and a later request reads it on a different kernel that expects compact_int, runtime must either:
  a) perform conversion at read-time (dequant->FP16) if kernel supports reads-from-FP16, or
  b) disallow cross-variant reuse and require re-generation of KV in target format (higher latency).
- KV alignment and addressability: KV stores must respect memory_alignment_bytes and quant_block_stride_bytes for kernels that operate on compact representations. Runtime must maintain alignment metadata in the cache index.
- Garbage collection and TTL: compact KV formats may be more expensive to convert; implement TTL heuristics to avoid excessive conversions when models are rapidly switching variants.

Fallback and compatibility rules (runtime policy):
- Preferred: use exact quant_family match and kernel capability match.
- Graceful fallback order: 1) exact kernel; 2) same quant_family different kernel (if supports_batched_kv_rewrite true); 3) dequant to FP16 and run on generic FP16 kernel (accept increased memory/latency).
- Deny-list: do not auto-fallback across quant families that have incompatible semantics without explicit config (e.g., GPTQ -> INT8 conversion should be opt-in).
- Observability: log fallback reason, source artifact, and conversion cost estimate. Emit metrics per-fallback for alerting.

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests per-kernel descriptor parser and compatibility matcher.
- Synthetic bench: run single-layer and multi-layer microbenchmarks across supported block sizes and compare latency and peak memory. Include dequant overhead measurement.
- KV cache integration tests: write/read pass for each supported kv_storage mode and cross-variant read tests (with expected fail/convert behaviors asserted).
- Regression suites: numeric regression tolerances for each quant family vs FP16 baseline. Define acceptable deltas per op (e.g., softmax post-layernorm output L2 < threshold).
- End-to-end smoke tests: full-model decoding with short and long sequences, verify latency SLOs and correctness.

Performance telemetry to collect:
- kernel_version, quant_family, block_size, batch_size, seq_len, latency_p50/p90/p99, gpu_utilization, memory_allocated, kv_conversion_ms, prewarm_hit_rate, fallback_count, error_rate.

Operational notes:
- Model artifact metadata should include quant_family and the capability signature of the exporter (exporter_name, exporter_version).
- CI: gated checks that require inclusion of kernel capability vector in release artifacts.
- Migration: when introducing a new quant kernel, provide a canary rollout flag and automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts.

Open questions and outstanding work:
- Standardize on the canonical descriptor key names and types across kernel vendors (proposal: use the descriptor contract in this doc).
- Define a compact on-disk representation for GPTQ/AWQ weight encodings to speed startup.
- Decide default KV storage across hosted vs dedicated: hosted default FP16; dedicated customers may opt into compact_kv for cost.
- Explore support for heterogeneous per-channel bitwidths in AWQ and scheduler heuristics for selecting layers to quantize.
- Seek baseline numeric tolerance specification per model family (Llama-like vs Mistral-like).

Implementation roadmap (high-level):
- Phase 1 (Q1): Implement kernel capability contract, descriptor parser, and scheduler compatibility checks. Add INT8 and FP8 descriptors for existing kernels.
- Phase 2 (Q2): Add KV conversion helpers, dequantation cost APIs, and prewarm hints. Run synthetic bench and add perf telemetry.
- Phase 3 (Q3): Integrate GPTQ/AWQ kernels with prewarm and fallback logic; extend regression tests.
- Phase 4 (Q4): Polished cross-variant KV optimization, autoscaler integration, and customer docs.

References and prior artifacts:
- Existing drafts: quantization-exec-path-specs-int8-fp8-gptq-awq-draft.json (v1, v2, v3)
- GitHub PRs and issues: see linked_artifacts above.

Appendix: Example kernel capability descriptor (flattened string form)
- quant_family=INT8;supported_block_size=256,512;requires_contiguous_weights=true;per_channel_scales=true;supports_decoder_cross_attention=true;supports_kv_fp_storage=FP16;max_seq_len_single_tensor=4096;fused_ops=gelu,layernorm,quant_dequant;supports_batched_kv_rewrite=false;memory_alignment_bytes=64;quant_block_stride_bytes=32;kernel_version=1.3.2

Sign-off:
Maya Thompson (eng-serving-runtime)
summary: Draft spec for execution path constraints and runtime behavior when supporting INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ kernels. Includes kernel capability contract, scheduling and KV cache rules, fallback policy, testing plan, and implementation roadmap.
